title: Ever heard of a C64 game called STIX?
author: Mallock78
selftext:
For years I've had this idea in the back of my mind: bring this game back to life.

Today I finally tried.

I asked AI to recreate the game that first hooked me into gaming. A couple of hours and a few iterations later, it was playable in a browser.

I was probably around eight years old when I first played it at my cousin's house on a Commodore 64. Somehow that game stuck with me for decades.

Claude rebuilt it as a neon Phaser version with a Qix chasing you around the arena, Sparx on the edges, a fuse that burns your line if you stop moving, territory capture, a score system, and CRT effects. The whole thing.

The original Qix (1981) was designed by a tiny team and built for hardware that was minuscule by today's standards. Recreating the core gameplay loop took one evening of prompting and iteration with AI.

You can play it here and post your high score:  
[https://stix.blinkki.com/](https://stix.blinkki.com/)

What's the game from your childhood that you'd instantly rebuild if you could?
